The game has a fundamental flaw in the gameplay. Attack direction is tied with movement direction so any weapons/attacks that rely on directional timing become useless since you are generally running away from everything, at least early on. The devs must release aim from movement and give an auto-aim feature or free aim, or this game will die a quick death. Thumbs down until at least that concept is fixed. I can forgive the market place since this is a F2P game, but not if the game doesn't even understand the genre it is trying to fit into.

AN FUN BULLET HELL/ROGUELITE GAME Overall I would say I recommend it, if you can get over the fact that you probably won't get the character you want if you play F2P and that you will definitely never max it if you get it by chance. Basically it's a Gacha-Vampire Survivors or Brotato. 100% Girlfriend approved XD Negative: -It's definitely a pay-to-fast (you could even argue pay-to-win but it's a solo game). -Semi F2P Friendly (you can definitely farm and progress without paying anything, but you will probably never have the character you want. You will need to build a character you have drop.) -Microtransaction for character, for equipment, for skin, for materials, so yeah. -Certain languages (French) son pas parfaitement translate, but nothing game breaking. Positive: -Good roguelite and mechanics overall, nothing new, really. -Artstyle is cute, fresh and slick. -Good diversity of active and passive weapons. Automatic shot. -Achievement give you goals and rewards, mostly material, but also a little amount of Gacha money. -Good variety of monsters, bosses and their mechanics. Can be a positive or a negative for some (for me, positive): -Farming! You will do and redo the maps in all their difficulties to farm the different materials in order to improve your character, your passive tree and your different pieces of equipment. Everything is semi-randomized every time you enter a map. But the drops are nothing impressive and you won't get any adrenaline rush.
Very addictive! Simple and dynamic at the same time. You upgrade your heroes, fight hordes of enemies and enjoy every level.

While the concept of this game is intriguing, the execution falls flat. The gameplay feels repetitive, and the graphics are underwhelming. It lacks depth and fails to engage, making it a disappointing experience overall.

The game is built around a pay-to-win model. While the gameplay itself is fun, it’s disappointing to see players treated as nothing more than a source of money. If you're a fan of action roguelikes, you'll eventually hit a brick wall, forcing you to either replay the same layouts at the same difficulty over and over for 15–20 minutes while gaining almost nothing—or pay to progress. The right way to build a strong community is by creating something truly great, and people will naturally stay and support your game. This kind of predatory monetization is just ridiculous.

I almost find it to be a very good game, but then have little parts of it that piss me off. I'm deciding to give up after the last 4 games didn't give me a speed boost option. I first use all of my bans, then I use all of my skills, level up 40x or whatever over the first 10 minutes, and movement speed never comes up. As a result the second boss just runs you down, and it's impossible to dodge everything. This doesn't happen on the earlier maps, but it does on the later ones. I just did the same map four times in a row without getting the movement speed offered once. There's literally no other way to survive it. I guess if I grind for a hundred hours there's a skill tree thing I can unlock that gives me a 7.5% movement speed boost... that might be enough to dodge a few of these? There's just something terribly designed about it when there's no way to survive except like this. Like I never feel like there's only one viable build or that one item is always absolutely needed in other games of this type. Meh. Anyway, except for when I'm ragequitting, I am impressed by the game. They do seem to update it and take criticism. Maybe they'll improve this somehow. I'll give it a +1 on the assumption this problem isn't what it will always be like... it just feels like that now. -_-
